rows.description: A hearing or deaf toddler may use signs or gestures for "more", "milk" or "all done" before speech. Deaf children exposed to a signed language from birth learn it on the same timetable as spoken languages.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler feeds a doll or makes a toy talk, trying out roles and feelings safely. Adults read it best as play and practice, not as a literal report of what the child wants or has done.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler bounces, claps and sings fragments of songs, showing joy, excitement or a wish to join in. The same swaying may also soothe a tired child, so context decides the reading.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, excitement, tiredness

rows.description: A toddler scribbles, smears paint or squashes clay for the sensory joy of making marks. Early marks show exploration and motor growth, not representational meaning, so praising effort beats asking what it is.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, resentment, hurt

rows.description: A toddler insists on a favourite shirt or refuses a hat, asserting choice and sensory comfort. Small choices support autonomy, and refusal is usually about texture or control rather than defiance.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler claps when others clap and waves along with a group song. Joining in shows delight and belonging, and imitation is how children learn shared signals.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler snuggles, pats or offers a kiss to a caregiver or pet. Affection is shown physically, and a child who does not want a hug still deserves respect for saying no.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A toddler giggles at a funny face or peek-a-boo, finding something silly and safe. Amusement depends on trust, since the same face from a stranger might cause worry.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, playfulness, anger, anxiety

rows.description: A toddler gasps and claps at bubbles or a surprise game, showing pleased surprise. The moment is brief, and repeating the fun lets the child feel safe delight.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, playfulness, surprise, trust

rows.description: A toddler squeals, bounces and beams when something delights them, feeling a burst of pleasure. Sharing the joy with a smile helps the child learn the feeling and how to tell others.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
